offence_severity: Life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 100/-, in default to suffer R.I. for 30 days
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to constriction of the neck
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 302/203/34 IPC; finally upheld under Section 302/34 IPC
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimony of PW1 as the sole eye-witness but found it unacceptable due to its improbabilities, doubts, and oddities inconceivable with normal human conduct.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly PW1, as unreliable and lacking in persuasion, with the testimony fraught with inconsistencies and improbabilities.
trial_duration: The incident was registered as a case of unnatural death and after six days of the occurrence it was converted into one under Sections 302/203/34 IPC. The trial court convicted the appellant and co-accused under Sections 302 and 34 IPC. The High Court affirmed the conviction. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and acquitted the appellant.
legal_representation: Krishnan Venugopal, Shivendra Singh, Ms. Deepanshi Jshar, Dharmindra Kumar Sinha for the Appellant. Shibashish Misra, Ms. Sylona Mohapatra for the Respondents.
investigation_status: FIR registered on 26.2.2000 under Sections 302/203 read with Section 34 IPC. Charge-sheet laid against the appellant and co-accused. Investigation included inquest, spot map, post-mortem, and seizure of evidence.

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted the appellant and co-accused under Sections 302 and 34 IPC.
appeal_history.high_court: Affirmed the conviction of both the appellant and co-accused.
appeal_history.supreme_court: Allowed the appeal and acquitted the appellant.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant and co-accused committed murder motivated by an extra-marital relationship, based on the testimony of PW1, who claimed to have witnessed the incident. The FIR was filed six days after the incident, and the High Court affirmed the conviction, accepting the prosecution's plea of motive of murder founded on the extra-marital relationship.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the testimony of PW1, the sole eye-witness, is wholly unbelievable, inconsistent, and fraught with improbabilities, doubts, and oddities inconceivable with normal human conduct. The defence emphasized that PW1 was intoxicated, did not raise any alarm during the incident, and remained silent for three days despite witnessing the murder, which casts doubt on his credibility.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that conviction can be based on the testimony of a single eye-witness if he or she passes the test of reliability, emphasizing the quality of evidence over the number of witnesses. It also emphasized that the standard of proof requires a prudent man's perspective on the existence or non-existence of circumstances.
precedent_relied_upon: Mahamadkhan Nathekhan v. State of Gujarat (2014) 14 SCC 589; Anil Phukhan v. State of Assam (1993) 3 SCC 282; Ramji Surya Padvi and Another v. State of Maharashtra (1983) 3 SCC 629; State of A.P. v. Patnam Anandam (2005) 9 SCC 237; Guam Sarbar v. State of Bihar (2014) 3 SCC 401; Lakeman Shah and another v. State of West Bengal AIR 2001 SC 1760; Narsinga Rao v. State of A.P. 2001 Crl.L.J. 515
